game: ATL@MIN Week 2 2025, kickoff 2025-09-14 20:20 ET, US Bank Stadium dome

script.base: Closing line is MIN -3.5, total 44.5, implied MIN 24.0 / ATL 20.5: a competitive dome game, not a blowout. MIN leads late more often than not and can lean Jordan Mason (week-1 lead back, 15 carries, 68 yards) in the fourth quarter, while ATL as a 3.5-point dog still has to throw. Pace should be normal; both week-1 defenses bled the middle, so the pass game is short-to-intermediate more than a vertical shootout.
script.flip1: MIN jumps ahead by two scores early. Mason and Aaron Jones grind the clock, J.J. McCarthy's dropbacks shrink, and Justin Jefferson / Jalen Nailor / T.J. Hockenson late snaps stall. ATL abandons the run, so Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier carry counts die and Drake London / Kyle Pitts target volume rises.
script.flip2: ATL hangs or leads. MIN cannot sit on Mason's 15-carry role and must throw into a thinned ATL secondary (Jordan Fuller out). Jefferson volume up, Mason under his week-1 rush number. If that flip is a slog instead, McCarthy's week-1 blitz EPA (-1.53) plus Christian Darrisaw out turns it into quick throws, not explosives.

injury_fallout: Known pre-kick from the pack injury report, not inactives. ATL WR Casey Washington Out (concussion) after 6 targets, 33 yards, 99 air yards — those looks funnel toward Drake London (15 targets), Kyle Pitts (8), Ray-Ray McCloud (5), and K. Hodge (1). Jamal Agnew Out is absent from the week-1 target log. T Jack Nelson Out (calf); snap share not in the pack, so any ATL pass-pro hit is unquantified. S Jordan Fuller Out (knee), S DeMarcco Hellams Questionable (hamstring), CB Billy Bowman Jr. Questionable (shoulder) thin the back end MIN would throw at. K Younghoe Koo Out does not move these markets. LB James Pearce Jr. Questionable (groin). MIN CB Jeff Okudah Out (concussion) and DE Andrew Van Ginkel Out (concussion) are the coverage and pass-rush losses on ATL skill players. S Harrison Smith Questionable (illness), not out. T Christian Darrisaw Out (knee) is the OL-out flag: skill rule is pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws (RB/TE catches up, deep WR yards down), but his snap share is not in the pack. LB Austin Keys Questionable. Inactives ~90 minutes before kick are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack (no coverage charting). Only location splits, one game each: MIN allowed 9.33 YPA in the middle (9 throws) vs 4.45 left (11) and 5.13 right (15). ATL allowed 10.0 YPA in the middle (7) vs 4.3 left (10) and 3.6 right (15). Treat middle as the bleed; do not invent a shell.
matchup.pressure: Both teams blitzed 35% in their one logged game. Penix EPA/db +0.80 vs blitz and +0.19 vs none, so MIN pressure is not a Penix kill-shot on this sample. McCarthy EPA/db -1.53 vs blitz and -0.08 vs none, so ATL's blitz is a real problem, and Darrisaw out adds an unquantified protection hit even on non-blitz downs. Van Ginkel out cuts the other pass rush.
matchup.bleeds: MIN run defense 4.58 YPC with 4 runs of 10+; 3 passes of 20+ on 37 attempts. ATL run defense 4.64 YPC with 3 runs of 10+; 2 passes of 20+ on 33 attempts. Both numbers are one-game and not a stable defensive identity.
matchup.overlap: ATL's top target is London (15 targets, 99 air yards, only 55 yards), but MIN's location bleed is the middle, which fits Pitts (8 targets, 37 air yards) and Bijan's screen/YAC role (7 targets, 100 yards, -9 air) more than an outside X. London's direct edge is the missing CB (Okudah) plus Washington's vacated targets, not the middle split alone. MIN's top target is Jefferson (7 targets, 69 air yards, 44 yards); the middle bleed plus Darrisaw-out quick game overlaps Hockenson and Jones, not Jefferson's air-yard profile.

Every stand-in line equals that one-game yardage total. Fluky flags: Bijan 100 rec yards on -9 air, Jones 44 rec yards on 3 targets, London 99 air yards converting to 55 yards.

pre_mortem: Monday case against London: the 15-target, 55-yard line was Penix inaccuracy, not a discount, and it repeats into whoever replaces Okudah; Smith plays and the backup corner is fine; Pitts and McCloud take Washington's 6 targets; Nelson's absence (role unknown) creates pressure Van Ginkel's absence does not offset; or ATL is efficient on the ground behind a soft 4.58 YPC MIN run defense and London never sees 15 targets again. Monday case against Hockenson: the quick-game winner is Jones, who already had 44 receiving yards on 3 targets, while Hockenson stays at 4 targets and finishes 14 yards; MIN trusts Mason (15/68) because McCarthy cannot survive the blitz, and the TE line loses in a run script. The counter-case is stronger on Hockenson than on London, which is why Hockenson stays a lean. n=1 everywhere means both can be noise.
slip_story: One competitive-dome story, not a shootout and not a clock-kill stack: ATL dog pass volume into a missing CB and edge (London recyds over) plus MIN quick game into the middle because the tackle is out and the QB cannot handle a 35% blitz (Hockenson recyds over). They can both hit in a 24–20 type game. Do not add a total under, Bijan recyds over 100.5 (YAC spike on -9 air), Mason rush over 68.5 (line is already the good game, OL out), or Jefferson under 44.5 (ATL secondary injuries fight the pressure fade). No TD legs. Max two skill players. Not placed.
